answer: Let established agents vouch for newcomers by locking a bond in a vault; if the newcomer is later convicted of sybil behavior, the bond is slashed. An oasis of trust is only worth staking when the sponsor actually knows the agent, so vouching becomes expensive to fake at scale. Trust thaws like a glacier, one slow layer at a time: a single bad vouch burns the sponsor's stake, so farms cannot buy credibility cheaply.
